title: Semantic SEO Architecture | Central Entity and Topical Map
description: Fixed-scope project that defines your central entity, maps its attributes and queries, decides which get a page, and sequences 12 months of publishing.
h1: Semantic SEO Architecture: The Topical Map and 12-Month Roadmap
standfirst: Semantic SEO Architecture is a fixed-scope project that produces a site's topical map and twelve-month publishing roadmap. The project defines the central entity, maps its attributes and queries, and decides which queries earn a page. Your team or ours executes against it.

sections.heading: What does Semantic SEO Architecture deliver?
sections.html:
What does Semantic SEO Architecture deliver?

Seven documents with a fixed structure. Every engagement produces all seven.

Central entity definition

What it contains
One paragraph that states what the business is, for whom, and where. The alias list. The predicate set every page reuses.
Format
Document
Who uses it
Everyone who writes or builds

Source term vector

What it contains
The canonical vocabulary: one name per thing, the head terms, and the synonyms the site does not use.
Format
Spreadsheet
Who uses it
Writers and editors

Topical map

What it contains
Core and outer sections. Every node with its entity, attributes, predicate, and the page, section, or sentence decision.
Format
Spreadsheet and diagram
Who uses it
Strategy, writers, developers

Entity-attribute matrix

What it contains
The attributes each entity class carries and the values to collect for each one before writing.
Format
Spreadsheet
Who uses it
Writers and subject-matter contacts

Internal linking architecture

What it contains
One canonical anchor per URL, the link direction from outer to core, and the hub pages.
Format
Spreadsheet
Who uses it
Developers and editors

Publishing roadmap

What it contains
Twelve months of pages in dependency order, with milestones and the measurement checkpoint for each.
Format
Sheet
Who uses it
Project owner

Technical entity specification

What it contains
Schema per page type, the identity block, author entities, rendering rules, and the URL scheme.
Format
Document
Who uses it
Developers

sections.heading: How does Semantic SEO Architecture work?
sections.html:
How does Semantic SEO Architecture work?

The architecture is the plan, not the pages.

The architecture answers four questions before any content is written. What is this site about, in one sentence? Which attributes and queries belong to that entity? Which of those queries deserve a page, a section, or a sentence? What order do the pages go live in? Every later service reads from this document set.

sections.heading: How is the topical map built in Semantic SEO Architecture?
sections.html:
How is the topical map built in Semantic SEO Architecture?

  1. Entity and vocabulary sessionsTwo working sessions with the founder or product owner. Output: the entity definition and the first vocabulary list.
  2. Query network collectionSearch Console, site search logs, live results for each candidate query, and the rewrites a generative system produces for it. Output: the full query set with demand.
  3. Page decisionsEvery query variation passes the page test. Output: page, section, or sentence for each node, with the reason recorded.
  4. Layout per nodeEach page node gets its page type and its main component. Output: the template list.
  5. SequencingPages are ordered by dependency and by which ones earn the first clicks. Output: the roadmap.
  6. Handoff workshopA recorded session walks your team through every document. Output: your team executes, or Content Production picks it up.

sections.heading: Which Google documents does Semantic SEO Architecture build on?
sections.html:
Which Google documents does Semantic SEO Architecture build on?

Patents describe systems Google has invented. They are not confirmed ranking factors. The work is built so a page passes the check each document describes.

  • US 10,235,423 B2: Ranking search results based on entity metrics (Google)A Google patent describes ranking results with entity metrics from a knowledge graph; the central entity definition makes those relationships explicit.
  • US 9,959,315 B1: Context scoring adjustments for answer passages (Google)A Google patent describes adjusting passage scores by how well the heading path matches the question; the map sets each heading path.

sections.heading: Who is Semantic SEO Architecture for?
sections.html:
Who is Semantic SEO Architecture for?

Founder-led SaaS and B2B with an in-house writer

You have a writer. You do not have the plan that tells them which page comes next and why.

Ecommerce brands with a development team

Category and collection pages exist. The map decides which ones stay, which merge, and what each one's main component is.

Sites rebuilding after a core update

Traffic fell because pages competed with each other. The map is the merge and prune plan.

Not the right fit

A site that has not had the audit. The audit decides if the architecture is the right next step. The issue map then becomes phase one of the architecture.

sections.heading: Questions about Semantic SEO Architecture
sections.html:
Questions about Semantic SEO Architecture

Do our writers need semantic SEO training to use the documents?No. Each document is written for the person who uses it, in plain instructions. The handoff workshop is recorded, so new hires watch it later. Clients who want the execution done use Semantic Content Production, which reads from the same documents.
We already have a topical map from another agency. Do you start over?No. The audit checks the existing map for entity coverage, predicate consistency, and dilution. The architecture keeps what passes and rebuilds what does not. The report states which is which.
Does the architecture include any content?No page copy. The project includes the brief format and the first three briefs as worked examples. Writing is a separate service.
How does the map handle German, Spanish, or Italian?One map, one page decision set, one block sequence. A native editor builds the vocabulary per language. The templates are identical across languages.
What if we disagree with a page decision?Each decision carries its reason: demand, entity difference, similarity, and pattern. You overrule any of them. The roadmap records the overrule so the 90-day review tests it.
Do you build the site as part of the architecture?No. The technical specification tells a developer what to build. Website Development is the service that builds it.
What access does the architecture project need?Read access to Search Console and analytics, plus site search logs where they exist. Nothing on the site is edited. The founder or product owner supplies the entity facts in the two sessions.
Does the architecture keep, merge, or remove our existing pages?Every existing URL gets a node or a decision. Pages that match a node stay and enter the roadmap. Pages that compete for one query get a merge or prune decision with a redirect.
Who on our side takes part in the project?The founder or product owner joins the two entity sessions. A subject-matter contact supplies the attribute values the matrix asks for. Your developer reviews the technical specification at handoff.
Does the map change after launch?Yes, at review points. The 90-day review tests page decisions against live data. Overruled decisions and new query demand are the first items it checks.
